## Purpose
Renders a single chat message (user or assistant) in the conversational chat lane, in a Claude/ChatGPT-style layout: bubble-free flowing text for AI replies with an avatar, a right-aligned bubble for user turns, collapsible `<thinking>` blocks, and a floating action bar (copy/edit/regenerate/TTS).

## Shape
- `MessageBubble` — the main export; branches into three render paths: a `ResultCard` for narrator turns carrying a generic `cardKind`, a right-aligned user bubble (with inline edit and file-attachment chips), and a flowing assistant turn (mode badge, `ProcessSteps`, thinking block, `AgentBlockStrip`, markdown body, `ArtifactCard`).
- `AgentBlockStrip` — coalesces a turn's `AgentEvent[]` into thinking/tool/file-ops blocks via `buildBlocks`, dispatching each block kind to `ThinkingBlock`, `renderToolBlock`, or `FileOpsSummary`.
- `parseThinkingBlocks` — extracts `<thinking>...</thinking>` regions from message content, separating them from the main prose.
- Uses `useSmoothText` to smooth the coarse, bursty deltas of streamed assistant replies into steady visual growth, and `useTextToSpeech` for the optional read-aloud action.

## Why this shape
Every render branch dispatches on generic message/block fields (`role`, `cardKind`, block `kind`) rather than a workflow-name literal, matching this codebase's stated invariant (SC-001) that UI must stay workflow-agnostic; the streaming-vs-static content split (`isStreaming`/`streamingContent`) exists because a historical message never grows while a live assistant reply does.
